question: What are the colors of signs that indicate the distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Yellow with black letters,b:Red with white letters,c:Black with white letters,d:Green with white letters.
note: Guidance and destination signs (including distance to exits) are green with white letters or symbols.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Stop in the middle of the road.,c:Pull to the right edge of the roadway and wait for it to pass.,d:Maintain your speed and lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, immediately pull to the right side and let it pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is true about signaling before turns, lane changes, or pulling from a curb?
options: a:You only need to signal during the maneuver,b:It is a good driving habit and is required by law.,c:It is only necessary if other vehicles are present.
note: You must signal your intentions in advance; South Carolina law generally requires signaling at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Beep your horn to warn them.,b:Assume they are in total control.,c:Expect the unexpected and be prepared for sudden movements.
note: Children on bicycles are unpredictable; be alert, reduce speed, and be prepared for sudden changes in direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss an exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your current lane.,b:Continue to the next exit or other safe location to turn around.,c:Stop and back up on the shoulder.
note: If you miss an exit, do not back up or make sudden lane changes; proceed to the next exit or safe location where you can turn around legally.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:Single solid white line.,b:Single broken yellow line.,c:Combination solid and broken yellow line.,d:Double solid yellow line.
note: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-way road means no traffic from either direction may cross the center to pass.

question: True or False: As vehicle speed increases, it takes longer to stop when reacting to another driver's unexpected actions.
options: a:Only on wet roads,b:TRUE,c:FALSE,d:Only with heavier vehicles
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and reaction distance, so it takes longer to stop at higher speeds.

question: Which action helps prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Drive above the posted speed limit.,b:Tailgate the driver ahead of you.,c:Relax
note: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm, focus on driving, allow plenty of travel time, obey speed limits, and be courteous to other road users.

question: When a vehicle with bright headlights comes toward you at night, what should you do to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Look directly at the headlights.,b:Stop until it passes.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Do not stare at oncoming headlights; glance toward the right edge of your lane so you can maintain course without being blinded.

question: True or false: While driving at night you may use only your parking lights instead of headlights.
options: a:Only on well-lit streets.,b:False.,c:Only during dawn or dusk.,d:True.
note: It is unlawful to drive at night using only parking lights. Headlights are required when visibility is reduced.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull behind pedestrians and pass them.,b:Continue because motorists always have the right-of-way.,c:Honk to encourage them to hurry.,d:Yield and wait for them to cross before proceeding.
note: At crosswalks yield to pedestrians; proceed only when it is safe and the crosswalk is clear.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what should other drivers remember?
options: a:Trucks require increased stopping distances and larger turning space,b:Trucks require less stopping distance than smaller vehicles,c:Trucks are quieter at night,d:Trucks always have the right-of-way
note: Heavy trucks need more stopping distance and wider turning room; avoid lingering alongside where the driver cannot see you.

question: May you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Only if you see no train coming.,b:Only on private property.,c:Only if you are in a hurry.,d:No
note: You must never go around a lowered gate. Obey lights, gates, and flaggers at railroad crossings to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a turn, what should you do?
options: a:Ignore signaling if no other vehicles are nearby.,b:Speed up to move through the turn quickly.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply at the last moment.,d:Activate your turn signal several seconds before turning.
note: To complete a turn safely, activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before you turn so other road users know your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're in the center lane of an expressway and continually passed on both sides, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to a lane on your right when safe.,c:Speed up to assert your position.
note: On multilane roads, drive in the right lanes unless passing or preparing for a left turn. Move right when appropriate to allow traffic flow.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk when using which device?
options: a:CD player,b:Radio,c:Seatbelt,d:Cell phone
note: Using a cell phone, even hands-free, is a major distraction that increases crash risk.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Turn on high-beam headlights.,b:Use low-beam headlights and slow down.,c:Use only parking lights.
note: Use low beams in fog (high beams reflect back) and reduce speed; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off safely.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Complete the pass with your vehicle fully in the left lane before returning.,b:Stay in the same lane because motorcycles need less space.,c:Blow your horn to force the motorcycle onto the shoulder.,d:Pass as closely as possible to avoid wind effects.
note: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing; never crowd it and make sure your vehicle is completely in the left lane before returning.

question: What should you do to increase safety when driving at night?
options: a:Drive at the posted daytime speed.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Look directly at oncoming headlights.
note: Night driving reduces visibility and depth perception; increase following distance and use headlights properly (low beams in traffic).

question: When double solid yellow lines mark the center of the road, what does that mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left,b:You may pass if you signal first,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction,d:Passing is permitted from the right
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing in both directions; they separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When backing up, the best practice is to:
options: a:Steer with both hands while looking into the side mirror.,b:Open the passenger door to gain a better view.,c:Only use the rearview mirror to back up.,d:Turn your head and look back over your shoulder while steering with one hand.
note: Always look behind you by turning your head and shoulders when backing up; steer with one hand to control the vehicle while observing.

question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?
options: a:Both lanes are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A dashed (broken) yellow line between opposing lanes means passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: If you must back up on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Signal and wait for someone to guide you.,b:Turn your head to look back before and while backing.,c:Back quickly to minimize time on the road.,d:Rely solely on side mirrors.
note: Always look over your shoulder and check behind the vehicle before and while backing up to ensure the way is clear.

question: What should a driver do if taking a non-prescription drug?
options: a:Read the drug's label for warnings about driving before operating a vehicle.,b:Drink alcohol to counteract drowsiness.,c:Continue to drive regardless of warnings.
note: Many over-the-counter medications can impair driving; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure about effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these statements about right-of-way is accurate?
options: a:You may make a right turn in front of a pedestrian in a crosswalk.,b:If two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time,c:Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.
note: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when making left or right turns; do not assume others will yield to you.

question: If your vehicle's wheels have run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn the front wheels slightly left to edge back onto the road.,b:Hold the wheel firmly,c:Turn the front wheels sharply to re-enter the pavement immediately.
note: If you run off the pavement, hold the steering wheel steady, release the accelerator, gently brake, slow, check traffic, and when safe, gradually steer back onto the roadway.

question: A driver whose left arm and hand are extended downward is signaling that they intend to:
options: a:Turn left.,b:Proceed slowly.,c:Turn right.,d:Stop.
note: When a driver's left arm points downward, it is a signal that the vehicle is slowing or stopping.

question: If you encounter an animal in the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Try to hit it to avoid stopping traffic.,b:Honk continuously to make it move quickly.,c:Slow and pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.,d:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.
note: Be cautious and pass animals slowly to avoid startling them and causing unpredictable behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: The usual speed limit in residential neighborhoods is 30 mph.
options: a:Only near schools.,b:False.,c:True.,d:Only during daytime.
note: Residential and urban speed limits are commonly 30 miles per hour, though posted signs determine the exact limit.

question: When you need windshield wipers for rain or snow, what else must you do?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beams).,b:Pull over immediately.,c:Switch to high beams.,d:Turn on interior lights only.
note: If conditions require wipers, you must also use low-beam headlights so others can see your vehicle.

question: What might be a possible effect of taking prescription medication while drinking alcohol?
options: a:It will make you more alert.,b:There will likely be no effect.,c:It can make you unfit to drive due to increased impairment.
note: Combining prescription medications with alcohol can increase impairment and make you unfit to drive; always check warnings and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

question: Do drivers need to stop for a stopped school bus when traveling in the opposite direction on a four-lane highway?
options: a:False,b:True (no stop required when traveling opposite on a divided four-lane highway)
note: On multi-lane highways with four or more lanes, drivers traveling in the opposite direction are not required to stop for a stopped school bus, though they should exercise caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposing traffic, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Only after signaling for at least five seconds.,b:When there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,c:Immediately regardless of distance.
note: Return to the driving lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is sufficient space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you driving too slowly?
options: a:When you are driving slower than 40 mph on any highway.,b:When you block vehicles moving at normal,c:When you do not pass other cars often.
note: You must not drive so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow or create a hazard.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee,b:Exercise,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol,d:Take a cold shower
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC; other remedies do not sober you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking facing uphill where there is no curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road,b:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road (right),c:Keep the wheels straight,d:Turn wheels toward the center of the road
note: If parked uphill without a curb, turn the front wheels toward the road edge so the vehicle will roll off the roadway if brakes fail.

question: When visibility is low because of fog, what is the proper driving technique?
options: a:Turn on interior lights to improve visibility,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights,c:Increase speed to clear the fog quickly,d:Use high beams for better viewing
note: In fog, use low beams and reduce speed; if visibility is extremely limited, pull off the road until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights to warn others,b:Reduce speed drastically,c:Check your rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind-spot vehicles,d:Turn on your hazard lights
note: Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure no vehicle is in your blind spot before changing lanes.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Apply the brakes hard,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control,c:Pump the brakes repeatedly,d:Turn off the engine immediately
note: If your vehicle skids, don't use the brakes; steer smoothly to recover control and keep the vehicle moving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate and you intend to change lanes or pass, what should you do?
options: a:Always use cruise control before changing lanes.,b:Stop on the shoulder first if tired.,c:Signal
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots. Do not stop on the shoulder except for emergencies.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be reduced,b:The combined effects of both substances may be increased,c:Nothing will happen,d:They cancel each other out
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can multiply impairing effects and increase harm and impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,b:Back up to the missed exit.,c:Roll down your window and ask for directions.,d:Continue to the next exit and return safely.
note: Do not back up or make a U-turn on the highway; go to the next exit and safely return to your intended route.

question: What must you do when you approach a stopped school bus on your side of a two-lane road with red lights flashing?
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.,c:Slow down to 10 mph and pass carefully.
note: Stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing; wait until the lights are turned off.

question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road when possible.,b:Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.,c:Signal and pull into the slow lane and stop there.
note: If your vehicle breaks down, get it off the road away from traffic if possible and turn on emergency flashers so other drivers can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not operating?
options: a:Proceed without stopping if the intersection looks clear.,b:Only stop if police are present.,c:Drive quickly through to avoid delays.,d:As an all-way stop: come to a full stop and yield before entering.
note: If signals are out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop, coming to a complete stop and yielding as required.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, what should you remember about trucks' stopping ability?
options: a:They have a smaller turning radius than passenger cars,b:They can stop as quickly as motorcycles,c:They require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles,d:They require less distance to stop than smaller vehicles
note: Trucks are heavy and need more distance to stop; leave extra space when driving near them.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, which of the following steps are appropriate?
options: a:Immediately stop in the middle of the road,b:Accelerate to maintain control,c:Turn sharply to reach the shoulder quickly,d:Remove your foot from the gas and do not immediately apply the brakes
note: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator, steer straight, slow gradually, and then pull off the road.

question: A large truck ahead is making a right turn on a street with two lanes in each direction. What is likely to occur?
options: a:The truck must remain in the right lane the entire turn.,b:The truck will always use the left lane to turn.,c:The truck may need to swing wide to finish the turn.,d:The truck can finish the turn in either lane.
note: Long vehicles have rear wheels that track a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks often need to swing wide on right turns to avoid clipping the curb or other vehicles.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate and swerve back immediately.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.,c:Slow down,d:Stop on the shoulder and remain there indefinitely.
note: Reduce speed without braking and carefully re-enter the roadway when clear of traffic and safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:When changing lanes,c:Only when pulling away from the curb.
note: You must signal anytime you move left or right: changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking spot or alley, or pulling next to or away from a curb.

question: True or False: By driving in South Carolina, you have consented to submit to chemical tests for intoxication if requested by law enforcement.
options: a:Only if arrested,b:False,c:True,d:Only if under 21
note: South Carolina's implied consent law means drivers agree to chemical testing for intoxication when requested by officers.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you need to stop quickly, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down hard and steer.,b:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.,c:Firmly pump your brakes.
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes helps stop quickly while maintaining some steering control. ABS-equipped vehicles require firm continuous pressure.

question: What color and text style do temporary construction and maintenance signs use?
options: a:Red background with green writing.,b:Green background with white writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.,d:Orange background with black writing.
note: Temporary work zone signs use orange backgrounds with black symbols or lettering to warn drivers.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Share the same following distance as behind cars always.,b:Follow closer because motorcycles stop faster.,c:Assume motorcyclists are more visible than cars.,d:Allow extra space in front of your vehicle.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and may be harder to see, so increase following distance to give yourself room to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the center of the street.,b:The lane nearest the right curb.,c:Any available lane.,d:The lane nearest the left curb.
note: When turning, begin from the lane closest to the direction you want to travel; from a one-way street a left turn should start from the lane nearest the left curb.

question: Which action disrupts smooth traffic flow?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a crash or unusual scene.,b:Avoiding needless lane changes.,c:Using public transit instead of driving.,d:Maintaining a steady speed with traffic.
note: Rubbernecking—slowing to observe crashes or unusual events—blocks traffic and should be avoided.

question: What do double solid yellow lines painted down the middle of the road mean?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction,c:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,d:Only passing by heavy trucks allowed.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean you generally may not cross the lines to pass, except in limited situations such as left turns when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is illegal and may result in fines and/or imprisonment?
options: a:Participating in or assisting a race on a public highway.,b:Speeding,c:Driving barefooted,d:Steering with one hand
note: Participating in or assisting a race or speed contest on a public highway is prohibited and can be punished by fines and/or imprisonment.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light you may:
options: a:No longer turn under any circumstance.,b:Still turn in the arrow's direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Have the right-of-way over oncoming traffic.,d:Only go straight.
note: When a green arrow becomes a solid green, turns are permitted but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following best describes a safe place to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a hill or curve where visibility is limited.,b:At any railroad crossing.,c:At a street crossing or highway intersection.,d:Only where you can see far enough ahead to be sure no oncoming traffic is present.
note: You may pass only where you can see far enough ahead to determine it is safe; do not pass on hills, curves, crossings, or where signs prohibit it.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the roadway after a stop, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to the transit vehicle and allow it to re-enter.,b:Honk to alert the driver.,c:Speed up to pass before it merges.,d:Remain in your lane and ignore its signals.
note: Yield to transit vehicles signaling to pull back into traffic after loading or unloading passengers by changing lanes or slowing as needed.

question: When entering a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and force other vehicles to make way.,b:Check behind you and the vehicle ahead,c:Stop in the lane until a gap appears.,d:Watch only the cars behind the gap.
note: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, be sure no vehicles are in the space you intend to occupy; check to the side and behind.

question: What does a solid white edge line that slants left toward the center of the road indicate?
options: a:The road narrows ahead (edge line angles into the roadway).,b:There is an intersection ahead.,c:You must turn left soon.
note: A solid edge line marking the road's edge that angles inward indicates the roadway narrows ahead.

question: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water; how can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Put on cruise control to keep a constant speed.,c:Slow down.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads; reduce speed in wet conditions to prevent tires from riding on a film of water.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to vehicles,b:Pedestrians must be yielded to by vehicles,c:Only pedestrians with signals have the right-of-way,d:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles
note: Vehicles must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk (marked or unmarked) unless directed otherwise by signals or officers.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red,d:Only stop if other vehicles are present
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign; stop fully, yield, and then continue when it is safe.

question: True or false: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.
options: a:True.,b:Only if the bus is on a driveway.,c:Only for commercial vehicles.,d:False.
note: Drivers must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading with flashing red lights and stop arm out, whether the bus is on public or private roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about making a right turn is correct?
options: a:When turning right onto a four-lane road,b:You should swing wide to the left when making a right turn.,c:You may make a right turn on red after stopping
note: After yielding to traffic and pedestrians, you may turn right on red unless a sign specifically prohibits it; stay close to the right curb and turn into the nearest lane.

question: If another vehicle suddenly cuts directly in front of you creating a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Swerve immediately into the adjacent lane.,c:Honk and slam on the brakes.
note: If a vehicle merges too closely in front of you, ease off the accelerator to create space; avoid abrupt braking or swerving unless necessary.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The condition of the pavement.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The vehicle's speed.
note: Braking distance is influenced by speed, brake and tire condition, and road surface; higher speed dramatically increases stopping distance.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Being on time.,b:Missing an exit only.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time and increases the risk of falling asleep at the wheel and being in a crash.

question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Maintain the same speed regardless.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to complete the pass.
note: When another driver wants to pass, slow slightly to increase the gap in front of your vehicle so the passing maneuver can be completed safely and quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a crowded freeway, what steps should you take to merge?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, use mirrors, check blind spots, and yield to traffic.,b:Stop on the ramp and wait for a large gap.,c:Merge at a much slower speed than traffic.,d:Assume freeway traffic will yield to you.
note: Accelerate on the entrance ramp to match freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to drivers already on the freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what is the appropriate driver response?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Always come to a complete stop regardless of other vehicles.,c:Yield to any vehicle approaching from the right and be prepared to stop to avoid a crash.
note: At an intersection without signs or signals, yield to traffic from the right and be prepared to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: How should you respond to an emergency vehicle with flashing lights in your area?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Stop your vehicle and block its passage.,c:Speed up to avoid the vehicle.
note: Yield the way by pulling aside or otherwise clearing a path so the emergency vehicle can pass safely.

question: Which statement about stopping for school buses is correct?
options: a:You only need to stop for a school bus if you see children crossing.,b:You must stop for a stopped school bus on any two-lane highway.,c:You must stop for a bus that is completely off the roadway in a passenger loading zone.
note: On two-lane roads, drivers must stop for stopped school buses with flashing red lights; laws vary for multi-lane roads and off-road loading zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a road with two or more lanes going the same direction, where should slower traffic generally travel?
options: a:In the left lane except to pass.,b:In any lane.,c:In the right lane except to pass.
note: Slower traffic should keep to the right; use left lanes primarily for passing or faster travel.

question: What is the best way to prevent a dangerous situation while driving?
options: a:Turn off the radio.,b:Constantly be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.,c:Keep your eyes focused only on the road ahead.
note: Continuously observing the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle helps you detect hazards early and gives you time to react.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what is the best immediate response?
options: a:Pull over immediately without slowing.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Apply the brake and hold it down.
note: Keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, slow gradually and brake lightly, then pull off the road when safe.

question: Which action will sober someone who has been drinking?
options: a:Getting fresh air,b:Drinking hot coffee,c:Drinking tomato juice,d:Allowing time for the body to eliminate the alcohol
note: Only time reduces blood alcohol concentration; coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not sober a person.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway compared to a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards earlier and allow more time to react.,b:Because it takes a quarter-mile to stop your vehicle.,c:To help you keep up with traffic.
note: On the freeway, higher speeds require looking farther ahead to detect hazards, merging vehicles, and changing conditions early.

question: For quick, controlled turns, where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel?
options: a:Both hands on the shifter,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel,c:One on top and one on the bottom,d:Next to each other on the top of the wheel
note: Placing both hands on opposite sides of the wheel promotes better control for quick, safe steering maneuvers.

question: Which driving abilities are reduced by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.,d:Only night vision.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination, increasing crash risk.

question: How should you respond when you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog at the edge of the roadway?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them,b:Stop and remain stopped until the person is safely away from the roadway,c:Wave them across the street,d:Slowly drive around them
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have priority; you must stop and yield until they are safely clear of the roadway.

question: Which action typically leads to hydroplaning?
options: a:Frequent sudden turns on dry roads.,b:Sudden stops on dry pavement.,c:Excessive speed on wet pavement.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot channel water away at higher speeds and lose contact with the road surface.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a motorist makes a left turn at an intersection, they should yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction:
options: a:Only at marked bike lanes.,b:False.,c:True.,d:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic, including bicyclists, when making a left turn; proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parked facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you set your wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels slightly to the left,b:Keep the wheels straight,c:Turn the wheels toward the curb,d:Turn the wheels away from the curb
note: When you park uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if brakes fail.

question: True or False: In foggy conditions you should use your low beam headlights.
options: a:Only use parking lights,b:Only use high beams,c:TRUE,d:FALSE
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect back off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: When weather suddenly changes, what should you do?
options: a:Be especially aware of vehicles behind you and adjust for their speed.,b:Adapt your driving to the new weather conditions.,c:Slow down when driving in rain or fog.
note: If weather changes suddenly, you must adjust your driving to match conditions. This includes slowing down in rain or fog and being aware of vehicles behind you.

question: When is it important to reduce your speed?
options: a:Only when other vehicles are speeding.,b:Only on downhill grades.,c:On narrow or winding roads
note: Always slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections or crossings, on wet or slippery pavement, in hills or blind curves, and when hazards are present.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you about the road?
options: a:You are on a one-way street.,b:The road is under repair.,c:Traffic is moving in both directions (two-way road).
note: Yellow centerlines separate opposite directions of traffic. A broken yellow line means passing is permitted when safe.

question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection,b:Continue and clear the intersection safely,c:Increase your speed to exit the intersection faster,d:Back up to avoid blocking traffic
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through promptly to clear it safely.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Trust stopped vehicles and pass cautiously.,b:Only check the road ahead.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that are stopped for no reason.,d:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
note: At places where people may cross or where traffic lines meet, always look left and right to make sure no one is coming before proceeding.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:You can check blind spots using only your rearview mirrors.,c:Having one outside mirror on each side eliminates blind spots.
note: Large trucks and buses have significantly larger blind spots; you should avoid lingering in those areas.

question: Which is NOT a factor used to determine stopping distance?
options: a:Perception time,b:Reaction distance,c:Braking distance,d:Steering ability
note: Stopping distance is based on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not part of the stopping distance calculation.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:Keep the wheels straight and do not turn.
note: When skidding, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to travel; as it straightens, correct the steering as needed.

question: In bad weather you should:
options: a:Brake hard to stop faster.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.,d:Drive in a low gear at all times.
note: In inclement weather, avoid sudden steering or hard braking; smooth inputs help maintain traction and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp correctly?
options: a:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.,b:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,c:Keep the same freeway speed while on the exit ramp.
note: Do not slow while still on the main travel lane; reduce speed after you have moved onto the exit ramp.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who is required to wear seat belts in a moving vehicle?
options: a:Only rear-seat passengers.,b:Only passengers on the driver's side.,c:All occupants of the vehicle
note: Seat belt use is required by law for all occupants in a moving vehicle; everyone must be properly restrained.

question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your speed,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and slow down,c:Ignore them if traffic is light,d:Speed up to get through the work zone quickly
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop; watch for workers, slow-moving equipment, and lane changes through the work zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a right turn on red (where permitted), you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping if the way is clear.,b:Increase your speed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Come to a complete stop
note: Unless posted otherwise, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After stopping at least 20 feet back from the intersection.,b:After coming to a complete stop before entering and verifying it is safe.,c:Only if no other vehicles are visible.,d:After slowing down but not stopping.
note: If there's a stop sign but no line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and go on only when safe.

question: Why should you allow an extra cushion of space behind a vehicle that cannot see its rear?
options: a:Drivers of large vehicles or those towing may not see vehicles directly behind them, so give extra following space.,b:Small passenger cars always stop faster.,c:Station wagons require more space than trucks.,d:It is safe to tailgate them to increase visibility.
note: Large vehicles or those towing trailers may not see cars directly behind; increase following distance to maintain visibility and safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Speed up without checking mirrors.,b:Check mirrors and blind spots,c:Honk repeatedly while passing.,d:Re-enter within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots, signal your intention, and return to your lane when it is safe and you can see the passed vehicle ahead in your mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are approaching a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Always come to a complete stop even if the way is clear.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a yield sign, slow or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to traffic already in the roadway you are entering.

question: Which sign of an aggressive driver might you observe?
options: a:Using turn signals consistently,b:Erratic,c:Driving slowly and yielding often,d:Pulling over to help other drivers
note: Watch for erratic, aggressive behaviors such as improper lane changes; avoid engaging and get out of their way.

question: Do bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers on public roads?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Bicyclists are generally accorded the same rights and duties as motorists and must obey traffic laws when on roadways.

question: True or false: Drivers are always required to stop for a stopped school bus when traveling on a two-lane road.
options: a:True.,b:False.,c:Only during school hours.,d:Only if children are visible.
note: On two-lane roads, drivers in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus that is loading or unloading passengers.

question: When steering, how should you hold the wheel and turn it?
options: a:Grasp the wheel tightly with your palms and thumbs tucked inside.,b:Use only your fingertips on the inside of the wheel.,c:Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel and use a firm but gentle grip
note: Place hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel, thumbs up, with a firm yet gentle grip using your fingers; steer using the outside of the wheel, not the inside.

question: If a cyclist is ahead in your lane and you want to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Treat the cyclist exactly like any other vehicle and pass in the same lane.,b:Tap your horn loudly to make them move over.,c:Wait until the opposite lane is clear and change lanes to pass
note: Treat bicycles as vehicles; before passing a cyclist in a narrow lane, wait until it is safe to move into the other lane to give adequate clearance.

question: When a stop line is present at an intersection, where must drivers stop?
options: a:Before reaching the stop line.,b:On top of the stop line.,c:Only if pedestrians are in the crosswalk.,d:Past the stop line to improve visibility.
note: At an intersection with a stop line, you must stop before the line or crosswalk and proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do when possible?
options: a:Hold your lane and refuse to change position.,b:Assert your right-of-way by maintaining speed.,c:Make room for merging vehicles.
note: When traffic permits, adjust speed or change lanes safely to allow merging vehicles to enter.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that lacks flashing signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Cross immediately as quickly as possible.,c:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing and ensure there is room to fully clear the tracks.
note: If there are no active warnings, look and listen for trains and do not cross until you are sure you can clear the tracks entirely; avoid shifting gears while crossing.

question: What problems do worn or bald tires create?
options: a:They improve fuel economy.,b:They prevent hydroplaning.,c:They have no effect on handling.,d:They can increase stopping distance and make turns more difficult.
note: Tires without adequate tread increase stopping distance, reduce steering control, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing procedure?
options: a:You only need to signal if another car is present.,b:Never check your blind spot when passing.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check mirrors and blind spots.,d:You can pass without signaling if on a clear road.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before lane changes, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before passing.

question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, using a cellphone, or changing the radio.,b:Only texting on a phone.,c:Driving without sunglasses.,d:Listening to the radio at low volume.
note: Anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving—such as eating, texting, or adjusting the stereo—creates distraction.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, which lights should drivers use?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low-beam headlights in rain or fog; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?
options: a:It drains the battery faster.,b:Vehicles behind you will follow too closely.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.,d:Other drivers may not see you.
note: High beams reflect off fog, mist, or heavy rain back into the driver's eyes and further reduce visibility, so always use low beams in such conditions.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed if you are near the top of a hill,b:You may cross to pass if you signal,c:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions,d:Passing is not allowed
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate no passing for traffic in either direction; they separate opposite-direction lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn toward oncoming traffic.,b:Toward the side of the road (right),c:Toward the center of the road (left),d:Keep them straight ahead
note: When parking downhill with no curb, turn wheels toward the road edge so a roll would move the vehicle away from traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,b:Flash your headlights to alert other drivers.,c:Check side mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,d:Immediately slow down without checking.
note: Check mirrors and the blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes to confirm the lane is clear.

question: When driving in areas where children may be present, what should you expect?
options: a:Children will only cross at marked crosswalks.,b:Children will always wait at the curb before crossing.,c:Children will avoid residential streets.,d:Children may run into the street without looking
note: Expect children to act unpredictably; slow down and be prepared to stop in neighborhoods and play areas.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Yield only to traffic on the left.,d:Continue at normal speed without looking.
note: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution; slow down, look, and go when it is safe.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Red lines.
note: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction; broken white lines mean you may change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A prudent driver should:
options: a:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all other drivers obey right-of-way rules.,d:Never yield even if it prevents a crash.
note: Right-of-way rules guide who should yield, but you should be prepared to yield your right-of-way if doing so prevents a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space needed to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:Only the presence of a stop sign.,c:Only your use of turn signals.
note: The gap you need to cross traffic safely depends on road and weather conditions plus the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.

question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Driving well below the flow of traffic.,b:Following other vehicles at a safe distance.,c:Inattentive driving.
note: Inattention is a leading cause of collisions; excessive speed and following too closely are also major contributors.

question: Which of the following can lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drinking coffee.,b:Eating high-fat foods.,c:Taking a cold shower.,d:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing else reliably speeds up sobriety.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Look and listen for another train on the other track before crossing,b:Drive around lowered gates if the first train has passed,c:Always assume it's safe to cross after the first train,d:Speed up to get across quickly
note: When there are multiple tracks, wait and be sure no other train is approaching from either direction before you cross.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light and indicates you should prepare to stop.,b:It always allows turns in the indicated direction.,c:It is not used on traffic signals.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protection for the indicated turn is ending; slow and prepare to stop as you would for a circular yellow light.

question: When you see a sign for your chosen exit, how should you respond?
options: a:Signal and move into the exit lane promptly,b:Reduce your speed once you are within the deceleration lane,c:Both signal and move into the lane and then slow to the posted exit speed,d:Ignore the sign until the last moment
note: When your exit approaches, signal, enter the exit lane, and slow gradually in the deceleration lane to the posted speed.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't impair your driving?
options: a:Have regular physical exams, know medication effects on driving, and drive within your limitations.,b:Ignore physical issues while driving.,c:Only avoid driving if you feel extremely ill.,d:Assume all medications are safe to take before driving.
note: Maintain fitness, be aware of medication side effects, and drive only when your physical condition allows safe operation.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline means passing is permitted from your side when it is safe to do so and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Honk before entering the intersection,b:Back up if someone is blocking you,c:Accelerate as quickly as possible,d:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection
note: A green light allows you to go, but you must first yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle in which situations?
options: a:Only at flashing yellow lights.,b:Only at intersections with stop signs.,c:At a stop sign,d:Only when pedestrians are present.
note: You must stop at intersections with stop signs, illuminated or flashing red lights, or any time a traffic officer signals you to stop.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb (left).,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb (right).
note: On an uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic if brakes fail.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Confirm that only adult passengers have buckled their belts.,b:Only buckle child passengers' belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt and make sure passengers have buckled theirs.
note: Develop a routine: buckle your seat belt and ensure all occupants are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not yet entered. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light,b:Come to a safe stop if you can do so,c:Sound your horn and proceed,d:Continue through without slowing
note: A steady yellow signal warns that the light will soon turn red; prepare to stop if you have not entered the intersection.

question: A motorist must stop for a school bus unloading children on a two-lane road:
options: a:Only if the bus is in your lane.,b:Only if children are on the roadway.,c:True.,d:False.
note: On two-lane roads, drivers in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus that is loading or unloading passengers.

question: What is the term for slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events, and why avoid it?
options: a:Rubbernecking; it causes traffic congestion.,b:Alert driving; it prevents collisions.,c:Defensive driving; it improves safety.,d:Sightseeing; it reduces delays.
note: Rubbernecking—slowing to observe crashes—creates congestion and can cause secondary collisions.

question: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your high beams at them,b:Glance briefly toward the right edge of the road,c:Stare at the bright lights to adjust faster,d:Keep focus on the centerline
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid direct glare, then resume scanning the road ahead.

question: A steady green arrow at an intersection generally allows drivers to:
options: a:Ignore the arrow if the circular light is red.,b:Merge into any lane in the arrow's direction without yielding.,c:Reverse direction.,d:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
note: A green arrow authorizes turns in the direction shown, but you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: A driver signaling with the left arm bent upward is indicating they intend to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Slow down.,d:Turn left.
note: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Watch for this signal and adjust your driving.

question: Why must drivers be particularly alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,b:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars.,c:Motorcycles rarely use their headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to hide in blind spots; they can be harder to see and it is difficult to judge their speed and distance.

question: On which surfaces does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways in good condition.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases on wet, icy, gravel-covered, or otherwise slippery surfaces.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Treat it as a yield signal and continue,b:Come to a full stop,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly,d:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, yield, and proceed only when safe.

question: When driving through work zones, you should:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed through the zone.,b:Change lanes frequently.,c:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop.,d:Increase your speed to clear the zone quickly.
note: Slow down, obey posted limits, and be alert for workers and changing traffic patterns in work zones.

question: Does the presence of double solid yellow lines in the center of the road allow passing from either direction?
options: a:Yes,b:No,c:Only when turning into a driveway,d:If no oncoming traffic is visible
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit crossing the centerline for passing in either direction, except to turn into driveways or entrances.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see your vehicle?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: When daylight begins to fade you should turn on your low-beam headlights so other drivers can see you. Reserve high beams for open roadways with no other traffic.

question: What does defensive driving involve?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents,b:Racing to avoid being cut off by other drivers,c:Following the vehicle ahead closely to reduce reaction time,d:Ignoring other drivers' errors
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking steps to avoid collisions before they occur.

question: Which of these is a prohibited parking location?
options: a:Within 100 feet of a driveway.,b:Within 45 feet of a fire hydrant.,c:On a sidewalk.
note: You cannot park on sidewalks. Other parking restrictions include within 15 feet of a fire hydrant and blocking driveways.

question: Are the effects of alcohol on reflexes and judgment dependent on the type of alcoholic beverage?
options: a:Effects are most pronounced with mixed drinks,b:Effects are less pronounced with beer than wine,c:Effects are less pronounced with wine than beer,d:Effects depend on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream
note: Impairment depends on blood alcohol concentration, not the type of drink consumed.

question: When is parking on the shoulder of a freeway allowed?
options: a:If you need to look at a map for directions.,b:Only in an emergency; otherwise parking on the shoulder is prohibited.,c:As long as you turn on your hazard lights.
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in an emergency. Pull off safely and use hazards if you must stop.

question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Rely on the inside rearview mirror.,b:Use your horn to detect vehicles.,c:Look over your shoulder into the appropriate blind spot.,d:Only use the outside rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Entering a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Using crosswalks when vehicles are present.,c:Waiting for vehicles to stop before crossing.,d:Using sidewalks when available.
note: Do not enter streets or crosswalks when vehicles are approaching; even with right-of-way, an approaching vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, which is the best immediate action among these?
options: a:Slam on the brakes hard.,b:Turn on your hazard lights as you take steps to safely stop the engine and slow down.,c:Blow your horn to warn others.
note: If the throttle sticks, turn on hazards, take your foot off the gas, shift to neutral if possible, brake gently, and turn off the ignition once safe to do so.

question: When making a left turn at an intersection, must you yield to an oncoming bicyclist?
options: a:False — bicycles must yield.,b:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.,c:Only if the bicyclist is wearing a helmet.,d:True — yield to oncoming bicycles in the same way as vehicles.
note: You must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to any oncoming motor vehicle when turning left.

question: You should never park a vehicle in which of the following locations?
options: a:Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.,b:Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.,c:Within 30 feet of a traffic signal or flashing beacon on the side of the roadway.
note: It is prohibited to park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing, within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, and within 30 feet of a signal light, stop sign, or flashing beacon on the side of the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering if you can do so safely; if not, continue through cautiously.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue without slowing.,c:Stop immediately no matter how close you are.
note: A solid yellow means prepare to stop; stop before entering if it is safe to do so, otherwise proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: True or false: When making an emergency roadside stop it is unnecessary to set your parking brake.
options: a:False.,b:True.,c:Only if on a flat surface.,d:Only if your vehicle has automatic transmission.
note: When stopping on the roadside in an emergency, set the parking brake and turn on your emergency flashers to alert other drivers.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane who is crossing the road, what must you do?
options: a:Pass close to them to move quickly,b:Always yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian,c:Only yield if they are at a corner,d:Tell them the best place to cross
note: Blind pedestrians have special protection; you must yield the right-of-way whenever they are crossing.

question: What is the recommended habit for checking blind spots when changing lanes or merging?
options: a:Check blind spots only when driving fast.,b:Turn your head to check over your shoulder to see the blind spot.,c:Rely only on side and rearview mirrors.
note: Always look over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes, merging, or pulling away from the curb; don't rely solely on mirrors.

question: For drivers aged 21 and older, at what BAC is it illegal to drive?
options: a:0.08 percent or higher.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older it is illegal to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your car be positioned?
options: a:In the right lane of the one-way street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the left lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the lane closest to the one you left, typically the left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you stop at a stop sign that does not have a marked crosswalk?
options: a:Before entering the intersection.,b:At the center of the intersection.,c:After you begin to enter the intersection if nothing is visible.
note: If there's no crosswalk or stop line, you must stop before entering the intersection and yield as required.

question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:
options: a:Only at marked crosswalks.,b:At all times.,c:Only when a crossing guard is present.,d:Only if accompanied by another adult.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times, whether or not a crosswalk is marked.

question: Which action can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allow extra travel time and be patient.,b:Speed up to keep up with traffic.,c:Ignore turn signals from others.
note: Allowing extra time, obeying speed limits, and signaling properly all help reduce stress and aggressive reactions.

question: If you approach a flashing red traffic signal, what is the correct action?
options: a:Treat it as a stop sign and come to a complete stop,b:Proceed without stopping if no vehicles are near,c:Wait until it turns green before moving,d:Slow down but do not stop
note: A flashing red light means stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:It is illegal to go around lowered gates, and you must obey stop signals and flaggers.,b:You may go around gates if you do not see a train.,c:All railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
note: You must obey all warning devices and never go around lowered gates; not all crossings have active devices so be cautious.

question: True or false: Alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes.
options: a:Only on weekends.,b:Only for drivers under 25.,c:False.,d:True.
note: Alcohol is a leading factor in fatal crashes because it impairs vision, reaction time, and judgment.

question: How are bicycles treated when used on roadways?
options: a:Bicycles are hazards and may be ignored.,b:Bicycles are considered vehicles and must follow the same road rules.,c:Bicycles must always use sidewalks.,d:Bicycles are not subject to traffic signals.
note: Bicycles are vehicles on the roadway and bicyclists and motorists must follow the same traffic laws.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the roadway, what is the correct action to take?
options: a:Slow down,b:Slam on the brakes immediately,c:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement,d:Speed up and swerve back onto the pavement quickly
note: Keep control, slow gently, and steer back onto the pavement when it is safe; avoid sharp or sudden moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed without yielding.,b:Stop completely before turning even if clear.,c:Sound your horn to warn pedestrians.,d:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic in the intersection.
note: You may turn on steady green unless prohibited, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop even if the way is clear.,b:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: Slow or stop if necessary, and give the right-of-way to any vehicle or pedestrian close enough to be a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal when approaching an intersection?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped as long as the light is flashing red.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, and go when clear.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your bloodstream can affect your:
options: a:Knowledge only.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Vehicle registration status.,d:Right-of-way privileges.
note: Any alcohol can impair judgment and coordination; impairment can occur even below legal BAC limits.

question: A driving distraction is defined as what?
options: a:Anything that improves your attention to driving,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to the road,d:A device that only affects passengers
note: A distraction is any activity or object that diverts your attention from driving, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street you should position your vehicle:
options: a:In any lane that is free.,b:Well left of the centerline.,c:Near the centerline.,d:Near the right-hand side.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, start from the lane closest to the centerline and turn into the first available legal lane, avoiding cutting the corner.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when entering a highway,b:Whenever other drivers are passing you,c:Only when a police officer is present,d:Whenever road or weather conditions make driving less than perfect
note: Reduce speed below the posted limit whenever visibility, traction, or other conditions make driving unsafe at the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:When the other driver waves you back.,b:After signaling for one second.,c:When someone in the other car honks.,d:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: Return when you can see both headlights (or the front) of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror, indicating adequate space.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility; pull over if visibility is extremely poor.

question: If a police officer stops you, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Speed up to get to a safer location,b:Drive to the nearest police station instead of stopping,c:Exit your vehicle and approach the officer,d:Pull over to the right side of the road and stop as far off the roadway as possible
note: When signaled to stop, pull as far to the right and away from traffic as you can, stop, and follow the officer's instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If several vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.,c:Yield to the vehicle on your left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if vehicles arrive at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: How many days do you have to notify SCDMV of a name or address change?
options: a:10 days.,b:15 days.,c:30 days.,d:45 days.
note: South Carolina law requires you to notify the SCDMV of any change of name or address within 10 days of the change.

question: In rainy weather you should be most careful when turning or stopping:
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.,d:Only during heavy storms.
note: Road surfaces are most slippery shortly after rain begins due to oil and dirt mixing with water, increasing stopping and turning risk.

question: Which statements about large trucks are true?
options: a:It is safe to tailgate trucks.,b:Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars.,c:Always drive beside a large truck for better visibility.,d:Trucks have larger blind spots than passenger vehicles and you should avoid driving beside them for long periods.
note: Trucks have large blind spots; avoid lingering beside or directly behind them where the driver cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one car length ahead.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: If you must park in an unusual area, what should you ensure about your vehicle?
options: a:Make sure the vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction,b:Park five feet from the curb,c:Park with your reverse lights on,d:Place your car in neutral and turn off the engine
note: Park so your vehicle does not create a hazard and is visible to oncoming traffic from any direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The larger vehicle.,b:The driver on the right.,c:The one who signals first.,d:The driver on the left.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and assume freeway traffic will stop for you.,b:Enter slowly and force traffic to adjust.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for an opening.,d:Signal
note: Use the entrance ramp to match the speed of traffic, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you're driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Rapidly pump the brake pedal,b:Slam on the brakes immediately,c:Take your foot off the accelerator and allow the vehicle to slow,d:Turn sharply toward the shoulder
note: If a tire blows, hold the steering wheel firmly, stay straight, lift off the gas, and slow gradually before pulling off the road.

question: What should be your first reaction to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on windshield wipers.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Increase your following distance only.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: Reducing speed is the primary response to decreased visibility and hazardous conditions; this gives you more time to react to hazards.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,c:Turn on your flashers and continue driving.
note: If an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop to allow it to pass.

question: On a two-lane highway, what must you do when you approach a stopped school bus with flashing red lights?
options: a:You may pass only if instructed by a pedestrian.,b:You may pass if the way is clear.,c:You must not pass until the bus turns off its flashing lights and resumes driving.
note: On a two-lane road, drivers from either direction must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to ensure safety?
options: a:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,b:Change lanes without signaling if clear.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move and check mirrors.,d:Rely only on the left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot and use mirrors and signals to verify it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traveling in a travel lane, you should:
options: a:Park briefly to drop off passengers.,b:Stop in the lane to check an address.,c:Keep moving until you can safely pull off the roadway.,d:Make a U-turn if you miss an exit.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane. If you miss an exit or turn, continue to the next safe location to pull off or turn around.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, yield to traffic and pedestrians in the circle, and enter to the right.,b:Speed up to enter before other vehicles.,c:Enter to the left and drive clockwise.,d:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: Approach slowly, yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians already in the roundabout, enter to your right, and travel counterclockwise.

question: Anything that requires you to do which of the following could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from driving.
note: Distractions that take your attention away from driving, cause you to look away from the road, or remove your hands from the wheel can lead to a crash.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which action might they legally take?
options: a:Cut through all lanes without regard for traffic.,b:Always wait on the sidewalk.,c:Use the left lane when preparing to or making the left turn.
note: Bicyclists may use the left lane to make a left turn; expect cyclists to behave like other vehicles on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp behave?
options: a:Assume they have the right-of-way and enter regardless of others.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate and merge when safe.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and merge when there is a safe gap; yield to vehicles already on the highway.

question: What must you do when facing a green arrow signal?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Turn only if no vehicles are behind you.,c:Yield to any vehicles,d:Wait four seconds before moving.
note: A green arrow indicates you may go in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, how should you use the brakes?
options: a:Use the brakes lightly,b:Pump the brakes rapidly,c:Apply full force to the brakes,d:Do not use the brakes at all
note: After a blowout, slow gradually by lifting off the gas and using the brakes lightly; do not brake hard or jerk the wheel.

question: When driving on wet pavement you should remember:
options: a:Roads are especially slippery right after rain begins.,b:Hydroplaning can occur at high speeds.,c:Give yourself extra space when stopping.,d:All of the above.
note: Wet road surfaces are particularly slick shortly after rain starts; hydroplaning is a risk, and you should increase following distance and brake smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left you should:
options: a:Accelerate slightly to make the turn faster.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Swing to the right of your lane.,d:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; only turn when the way is clear.

question: Which definition best matches distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Driving while tired only.,c:Anything that takes your eyes,d:Only using a cellphone while driving.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that diverts attention from driving—visual, manual, or cognitive distractions.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway you should:
options: a:Drive in the truck's blind spot to stay out of traffic.,b:Always pass on the right.,c:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,d:Follow closer to reduce wind effects.
note: Trucks have larger blind spots and longer stopping distances, so leave extra following distance when behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You may not pass when a solid yellow line is on your side of the centerline; passing is allowed only when the broken line is on your side.

question: At a red light that displays a green arrow in your direction, you may proceed if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait for the circular green light.,c:You yield only to oncoming vehicles.,d:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: A green arrow indicates you may turn in the arrow's direction if you are in the proper lane. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection before turning.

question: If oncoming headlights blind you at night, what is the correct action?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch to high beams to see better.,c:Look directly at the lights to get used to them.,d:Close your eyes briefly.
note: Glance to the right edge of the road rather than at the oncoming lights to keep your vehicle safely positioned until the vehicle passes.
